question: What can be established about Western/Bacusínare me'líame in the 1974 title Regá me'líame ju ye ajágame without deriving a word-level gloss from the Spanish title?

target_document.author: Albino Mares Trías
target_document.institutional_metadata_source: Colecciones Digitales de El Colegio de México

lexical_root.source: Compendio básico de la gramática ralámuli, 1997

participial_nominalization.source: Compendio básico de la gramática ralámuli, 1997, Verbo + Sufijo = Nombre
participial_nominalization.metalinguistic_statement: The Compendio explicitly states that -ame/-me also functions as a participle.

passive_domain.source: Compendio básico de la gramática ralámuli, 1997, El Pasivo
passive_domain.metalinguistic_statement: A combination of passive forms may be used, such as -li with -ru.
passive_domain.same_root_context: Translations of 'El hombre fue matado por el oso' use the me'/mi' kill root and are explicitly glossed mata-pasivo across varieties including Baja and Baja-TB.
passive_domain.ocr_warning: The digitized strings in the passive examples are graphically corrupted (e.g. lflru-like sequences). Do not normalize their exact spelling from OCR.

finite_control.assessment: Direct Western finite form in a killing context.

derived_family.assessment: Western corpus directly displays a productive me'li- surface family. These forms are not automatically segmented as root + -li.

constructional_control.assessment: me'líame is a second lexical-root member of a recurrent Western/Baja ...li(a)me + ju surface construction.

support: The same root me'á is explicitly documented with participial -ame: me'á + -ame = me'áme.
The same root is used in the Compendio passive paradigm, and the grammar explicitly says passive -li can combine with -ru.
Baja-TB independently allows a passive-marked predicate followed by nominalizer -me: rewa-lí-me.
Western 1974 me'líame contains the expected surface sequence and occurs before copula ju.
The recurrent Western ...li(a)me + ju construction has at least two lexical families.
problems: The 1974 title itself has no interlinear segmentation.
The exact passive strings in the digitized Compendio are OCR-corrupted.
Western me'li- may involve stem allomorphy or morphophonology in addition to concatenative -li.

support: Western TAC has many surface me'li- forms in multiple inflectional environments.
Other Rarámuri varieties also show stem-shape alternations under morphology, so visual li need not always be an independently segmentable suffix.
problems: The Compendio explicitly identifies passive -li as a grammatical resource and applies passive morphology to the same me'á root.
A purely lexical-stem account would need to explain why the resulting form aligns with independently documented passive + nominalizer architecture.

competing_analyses.analysis: historically different or lexicalized structure not reducible to M1/M2
support: The target form lacks direct segmentation and the 1974 orthography may preserve distinctions not transparent in later sources.
problems: It currently has less positive explanatory support than M1/M2.

current_assessment.preferred_working_analysis: M1, with M2 retained as a serious morphophonological alternative

relevance_to_newalime.assessment: me'líame provides an independent second Western lexical-root replication in which both the internal li-domain and outer -ame domain are source-supported on the same lexical root. This substantially strengthens the constructional analysis of newálime without proving identical morphology in the two words.

next_tests: Recover the full 1974 Bacusínare text and locate me'líame in sentence context beyond the title.
Search Western grammar/dictionary materials for an explicit me'á/me'li paradigm and segmentation.
Determine whether Western finite me'ale and me'li- alternations are governed by a documented -li morpheme or stem allomorphy.
Search additional Albino Mares Trías texts for independent me'liame or other root+liame tokens.
epistemic_rule: Same-root evidence for passive morphology and participial -ame can raise morphological plausibility, but it cannot substitute for direct segmentation of the target token. OCR-corrupted strings must never be silently normalized.
